answer: The timber escrow is released only against a knoll receipt, and the ripple audit re-checks every release at replay. Submitting an answer locks 12 units of stake that stay frozen until the verdict is sealed, and a junk verdict burns the stake instead of returning it. Because the lock is per submission rather than per identity, running 213 aliases means carrying 133 concurrent locks that earn nothing while frozen. That is 31 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
